occasion.name: Nativity of the Lord - Proper I

notes.text: The people — Israel and Judah. Darkness - The expression is general and so may well comprehend both calamity and ignorance, idolatry and profaneness, in which those parts were eminently involved. Have seen - Shall see at the coming of the Messiah.

Thou hast — Thou hast made good thy promise to Abraham concerning the multiplication of his seed, by gathering in the Gentiles to the Jews. Before thee - In thy presence, and in the place of thy worship.

The yoke — His burdensome yoke. The staff - The staff or staves by which he was forced to carry burdens upon his shoulders. The rod - Wherewith he beat him. Oppressor - Of all his oppressors, but especially of sin and the devil. As - When God destroyed the Midianites in so admirable a manner by three hundred men.

Noise — With the triumphant exclamations of the conqueror, and the bitter Lamentations of the conquered, and the different cries of the same persons, sometimes conquering, and sometimes conquered. Blood - With great difficulty and slaughter. But - But this victory which God's people shall have over all their enemies, shall be more terrible to their adversaries, whom God will utterly consume, as it were by fire.

For — Having spoken of the glorious light, and joy, and victory of God's people, he now proceeds to shew the ground of it. Us - Unto us Jews, of whom Christ was born, and to whom he was primarily sent. A child - The Messiah by the consent of interpreters, not only Christian, but Jewish: for so the ancient Hebrew doctors understood the place, and particularly the Chaldee paraphrast; although the latter Jews, out of opposition to Christ, wrest it to Hezekiah. Which extravagant conceit, as it hath no foundation in this or any other text of scripture, so it is fully confuted by the following titles, which are such as cannot without blasphemy and nonsense be ascribed to Hezekiah, nor indeed to any mere mortal man, as we shall see. Is born - Or, shall be born, as the prophets generally speak. The government - Of God's people, to whom he is given. Shoulders - Upon him, or in his hands. He mentions shoulders, because great burdens are commonly laid upon men's shoulders. His name - This is not to be taken for a description of his name, but of his glorious nature and qualities. Wonderful counsellor - And so Christ is, because he hath been the counsellor of his church in all ages, and the author and giver of all those excellent counsels delivered not only by the apostles, but also by the prophets, and hath gathered and enlarged, and preserved his church, by admirable counsels and methods of his providence, and, in a word, hath in him all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge, Colossiansii, 3. Mighty God - This title can agree to no man but Christ, who was God as well as man, to whom the title of God or Jehovah is given, both in the Old and New Testament. And it is a true observation, that this Hebrew word El is never used in the singular number, of any creature, but only of the almighty God. The father - The father of eternity. Who, though as man he was then unborn, yet was and is from everlasting to everlasting.

No end — His peaceable and happy government shall be extended to all the ends of the earth. The throne - Which was promised to David, and to his seed forever. For ever - From the beginning of it to all eternity. The zeal - This great work shall be brought to pass by almighty God, out of that fervent affection which he hath to his own glory, to the honour of his son, and to his people.

glossa.text: *In the region of the shadow of death.* ((ID.)) They are in the shadow of death who still live in sins: *in the region of the shadow of death,* they who have already gone down to the lower regions with dead works.

*Thou hast not magnified the joy.* To us, concerning the salvation of the Jews; for although they rejoice over the conversion of the Gentiles, yet they grieve over the rejection of the Jews.

 *They shall rejoice before thee,* etc. The prophet to Christ, concerning the disciples.

*For the yoke.* ((ID.)) Christ has a yoke, but a sweet one; the devil also, but one unbearable by its burden. And Christ has the princedom upon his shoulder, upon which he bore the cross; and the devil upon his shoulder a rod, wherewith he is proud.

*Of the exactor.* Of him, namely, that exacts. For daily he exacts from posterity, with usury, the coin of sin which he committed to the first man.

*For every violent plundering.* ((ID.)) As if he should say: The human race which the devil has plundered, the Lord shall take away from him violently, that is, powerfully, and shall thrust him down with tumult into hell. Whence both of him and of his members it is said: *Their memory hath perished with a noise ((Psal. IX))*.

*The garment mingled.* ((ID.)) The devil, who is full of the blood of all, who is a murderer from the beginning; or men, with whom the devil is clothed about as with a garment, whose hands are full of blood.

*A child is born to us.* Not to the Jews, to us, etc., *as far as* but to them that see not, he seems not to rise. 

*The princedom upon his shoulder.* ((ID.)) While he was being led to the gibbet, he bore the cross, upon which he merited the princedom.

((ID.)) The Seventy: *The angel of great counsel.* Which is not had in the Hebrew; but, terrified by the majesty of the names, they did not dare to say of the child that he was openly to be called God. Therefore for these six names they put this, *the angel of great counsel.*
*The zeal of the Lord.* ((ID.)) The prophecy began from Emmanuel, where it is said: *Ask thee a sign from God.* Here it is ended.

notes.text: O sing — Upon this new and great occasion, not the removal of the ark, but the coming of the Messiah.
Gods — The gods of the nations, as the next verse expounds it.
Before him — In his presence.
Beauty — Cloathed with all the gifts and graces, which are necessary in God's worship.
Reigneth — God hath now set up his kingdom in the world. Established - The nations of the world shall by the means of it enjoy an established and lasting peace.

Before — At the presence and approach of their Lord and Maker. Cometh - To set up his throne among all the nations of the earth. Christ is the Alpha and Omega in this psalm. His government speaks terror to his enemies, ver. 1-7. And comfort to his friends, whom he preserves and delivers, ver. 8-12.

glossa.text: *Sing ye to the Lord.* ((ID.)) He forewarned the Jews in the preceding psalm that, their hardness being laid aside, they should believe Christ; but because it was to abide, he now admonishes all the Gentiles. The second psalm concerning both comings. First he speaks to the prelates, that they themselves should sing and declare. *A new canticle.* ((AUG.)) Cupidity sings the *old,* etc., *as far as* whosoever shall have entered in, is without.

*To the Lord, and bless.* ((HIER., CASS.)) Thrice to the Lord, for the distinguishing of the trinity of persons; because the praise of Christ is the honor of the Trinity. And there is the figure epimone, that is, a frequent repetition of the same sentiment, which heightens it unto praise or unto blame.

*Declare ye.* He speaks to the prelates, declare, because thus grows the building of the house. *From day to day.* ((CASS.)) The Old and the New Testament are days, which grow bright by the eternal sun, the one foretells, the other shows the thing done. ((HIER.)) He declares therefore from day to day, etc., *as far as* by which the feet of our affections are fenced from the thorns of the vices.
*Great is the Lord.* ((AUG.)) Made little, because you are little, understand him great, and you shall be great in him.
*He made the heavens.* ((ID.)) The apostles and the angels, whence if he made the heavens and the angels, then the apostles also, who command the demons.

*In the sight.* For such men, namely those confessing and just, behold him themselves, and are beheld by him. *Holiness and magnificence.* ((AUG.)) As if he should say: He who wishes to be magnificent and mighty, as the angels are, let him first be holy, which comes to pass from him who sanctifies: for of thyself thou canst not be holy. When therefore he sanctifies, a man is made holy, and so magnificent.

*Bring to the Lord, ye kindreds.* ((CASS.)) The second part, where he speaks to the subjects, etc., *as far as* that none be excepted, native or stranger. *Glory.* ((ID.)) Because a man converses well, in whom God is glorified. *Honor.* When from good things thanks are rendered, whence, *There was not found who would give honor to God, but this stranger. Into the courts.* ((ID.)) The *courts,* the prophets or the apostles, by whom there is a going to the Lord; from the courts, that is, the prophets or the apostles, there is a coming into the court of the Catholic Church, where the majesty is adored. ((AUG.)) Or, Enter ye into the court, that is, into the doctrine of the prophets and the apostles.

*Adore ye the Lord in the court,* etc. That is, in the Catholic Church, or by the *courts,* prophecy; by the *court,* the Gospel. *Let it be moved.* All being admonished, he desires that they be moved. As if he should say, enter in and adore, you that are good. *But the earth,* etc. *The whole earth.* ((CASS.)) Not some part of it; therefore, lest anyone say: *Lo, here is Christ to be there,* he subjoins, *For he hath corrected the world of the earth,* etc.

*Say ye among the nations.* ((ID.)) That he reigned and corrected and judged. *He hath reigned.* Another reading: *He hath reigned from the wood ((Matth. XIII))*. ((AUG.)) Of the cross, by which man passes over the *sea,* and becomes a *world* which is not moved.

*The peoples in equity,* etc. Others add, *And the nations in thy wrath.*

((CASS.)) The peoples therefore, that is, the good, he shall judge in equity, but the nations, that is, the wicked, in his wrath.

*Then shall they rejoice.* ((CASS., HIERON.)) *Then,* when he shall correct, etc., *as far as* because he is come, that is, he shall come to judge the earth. *Because he is come.* ((AUG.)) First he came in the Church, in the clouds, that is, in the apostles, and filled the whole world; whence: *From henceforth you shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds ((Matth. XXVI))*: he who believes that coming shall rejoice in the last coming.

*He shall judge the world.* ((CASS.)) He generally includes every man, to be judged according to the equity of God. But how he is judged he sets forth by saying, *the peoples in truth,* because in the separation there shall be two peoples, to whom he shall give the sentence of truth, so that some go into life, others into punishments. ((AUG.)) By *the world* he means all the sons of Adam, etc., *as far as* the south.

notes.text: The saving grace of God — So it is in its nature, tendency, and design. Hath appeared to all men - High and low.

Instructing us — All who do not reject it. That, having renounced ungodliness - Whatever is contrary to the fear and love of God. And worldly desires - Which are opposite to sobriety and righteousness. We should live soberly - In all purity and holiness. Sobriety, in the scripture sense, is rather the whole temper of a man, than a single virtue in him. It comprehends all that is opposite to the drowsiness of sin, the folly of ignorance, the unholiness of disorderly passions. Sobriety is no less than all the powers of the soul being consistently and constantly awake, duly governed by heavenly prudence, and entirely conformable to holy affections. And righteously - Doing to all as we would they should do to us. And godly - As those who are consecrated to God both in heart and life.

Looking — With eager desire. For that glorious appearing - Which we hope for. Of the great God, even our saviour Jesus Christ - So that, if there be (according to the Arian scheme) a great God and a little God, Christ is not the little God, but the great one.
Who gave himself for us — To die in our stead. That he might redeem us - Miserable bondslaves, as well from the power and the very being, as from the guilt, of all our sins.

glossa.text: *For there hath appeared.* As if he should say: All are to be admonished, because Christ was born for all; he excluded no one. Or, *Grace,* that is, Christ who is the grace of God. Or, *the grace of God and of the Saviour,* etc., that is, God and our Saviour, namely the Son of God, who, although he be invisible in the form of God, yet by grace hath appeared in the form of a servant.

*And the coming of the glory of the great God,* etc. Who will come not in infirmity as before, but in glory and power, about to give rewards according to merits: who in his first coming was so humble that he not only instructed, but even gave himself. *A pursuer of good works,* etc. Because for this Christ redeemed us, that, pursuing a pure life and filled with good works, we may be able to be heirs of God.

notes.text: That all the world should be enrolled — That all the inhabitants, male and female, of every town in the Roman empire, with their families and estates, should be registered.
When Cyrenius was governor of Syria — When Publius Sulpicius Quirinus governed the province of Syria, in which Judea was then included.

And while they were there, the days were fulfilled that she should be delivered — Mary seems not to have known that the child must have been born in Bethlehem, agreeably to the prophecy. But the providence of God took care for it.

She laid him in the manger — Perhaps it might rather be translated in the stall. They were lodged in the ox stall, fitted up on occasion of the great concourse, for poor guests. There was no room for them in the inn - Now also, there is seldom room for Christ in an inn. Matt. i, 25
To you — Shepherds; Israel; mankind.

Glory be to God in the highest; on earth peace; good will toward men — The shouts of the multitude are generally broken into short sentences. This rejoicing acclamation strongly represents the piety and benevolence of these heavenly spirits: as if they had said, Glory be to God in the highest heavens: let all the angelic legions resound his praises. For with the Redeemer's birth, peace, and all kind of happiness, come down to dwell on earth: yea, the overflowings of Divine good will and favour are now exercised toward men.
For all the things that they had heard — From Mary; as it was told them - By the angels.

glossa.text: *There went out a decree from Caesar. ((AUG., BED.))* Augustus reigned in peace for twelve years about the nativity of Christ, etc., *as far as* here first Judaea was made tributary to the Romans.

*The first. ((BEDA.))* Already at various times very many parts of the world are read to have been enrolled, but this is the first of those which took in the whole world; and it is a profession of minds, because no one is shut out. Or certainly it then first began, when Cyrinus was sent by Caesar into Syria, to be an assessor of patrimonies.

*Nazareth. ((ID.))* Daily the Lord is conceived in Nazareth, etc., *as far as* the insistence of the teacher who speaks avails nothing unless it has received the increase of help from above that it may be heard.

*And it came to pass.* The Lord willed to be conceived in one place and born in another, that he might the more easily escape the fury of the plotting Herod. The humility of Christ is commended, because he willed not only to be made flesh, but even to be born at that time in which, as soon as he was born, he should be made subject to Caesar's census for the sake of our deliverance.

*She wrapped him up in swaddling clothes.* He is clothed in mean cloths, that we might receive the robe of immortality. His hands and feet are bound fast, that our hands may be directed to working well, and our feet into the way of peace; he was made a little one, that we might be perfect.
*And there were shepherds. ((BEDA.))* The highest shepherd being born, the shepherds from the snares of the night, etc., *as far as* upon whom the divine grace flashes more abundantly.

*And behold an angel of the Lord. ((ID.))* The citizens of heaven bear witness to the Lord both as to be conceived, and as conceived, and as born, that they may both sufficiently instruct mortals and pay their own service to their author.

*An infant wrapped in swaddling clothes. ((ID.))* The infancy of the Saviour has been pressed home by frequent testimonies both of the angels and of the evangelists, that it may be fixed the more deeply in our minds what he was made for our sake: in which his humility is commended: *Because, whereas he was rich, he became poor for us, that by his own poverty he might enrich us ((II Cor))*.

*And on earth peace.* When by sinning we were strangers to God, the angels reckoned us strangers; but because we have known our king, the angels have recognized us as their own fellow citizens. And the angel fears to be adored by a human nature which he beholds in his own king.

*To men of good will. ((BEDA.))* Who receive Christ when born; not to those who at the hearing of his nativity were troubled and persecuted him. *There is no peace to the wicked, saith the Lord ((Isa. XLVIII))*.
*And they came with haste. ((BEDA.))* The presence of Christ is not to be sought with sloth, etc., *as far as* they will find him as it were in a manger.
*And seeing.* It is the vision or knowledge of God, and this alone is the life of men, that they should know the true Father, and that Jesus Christ, whom he sent, is one God.

*They wondered.* They wonder both at the mystery of the incarnation and at so great a testimony of shepherds, who did not know how to feign what they had heard, but with a simple eloquence proclaimed true things. But the Lord appointed not orators but fishermen to preach the Gospel. So too in the Old Testament he ordained shepherds as the messengers of his dispensation. Therefore the testimony of the shepherds is not to be lightly esteemed.

*And returning,* etc. ((BEDA.)) Thus spiritual shepherds, while others sleep, are borne up by contemplating heavenly things, etc., *as far as* when they say: *Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to men of good will.*

echoes.text: He will redeem Israel from all their sins.
echoes.note: 'Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity' (v.14) closely tracks 'he shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.' The pairing of redemption with deliverance from all iniquity/lawlessness is a near-verbal dependence.

echoes.text: Now therefore, if you will indeed obey my voice, and keep my covenant, then you shall be my own possession from among all peoples; for all the earth is mine;
echoes.note: 'Purify for himself a people for his own possession' (v.14) draws on 'you shall be my treasured possession (peculiar people) above all peoples.' The covenant election of a treasured people is reapplied to the church redeemed by Christ.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God. Yahweh your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth.
echoes.note: 'A people for his own possession' (v.14) echoes Israel as 'a holy people unto the LORD, a peculiar people unto himself, above all peoples.' Part of the Deuteronomic treasured-people cluster behind v.14.

echoes.text: For you are a holy people to Yahweh your God, and Yahweh has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth.
echoes.note: Restates the election of Israel as a 'peculiar people' / treasured possession, directly informing the 'people for his own possession' language of v.14.

echoes.text: Yahweh has declared this day that you are a people for his own possession, as he has promised you, and that you should keep all his commandments.
echoes.note: 'The LORD has avouched you this day to be a peculiar people unto himself' supplies the covenant-possession formula reused in v.14, here tied to keeping his commandments (cf. 'zealous for good works').

echoes.text: Yahweh’s glory shall be revealed, and all flesh shall see it together; for the mouth of Yahweh has spoken it.”
echoes.note: 'The grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all men' (v.11) and the 'appearing of the glory' (v.13) draw on the revelation of the LORD's glory which 'all flesh shall see together.' The universal scope of salvation/glory revealed is Isaianic.

echoes.text: My son, don’t despise Yahweh’s discipline, neither be weary of his reproof: for whom Yahweh loves, he reproves; even as a father reproves the son in whom he delights.
echoes.note: Grace 'instructing/training us' (paideuō, v.12) to renounce ungodliness invokes the divine discipline tradition: the LORD chastens/instructs the one he loves as a father his son. The pedagogical grace of Titus is framed in this wisdom-discipline idiom.
echoes.lxxText: My son, despise not the chastening of the Lord; nor faint when thou art rebuked of him: for whom the Lord loves, he rebukes, and scourges every son whom he receives.

echoes.text: You shall consider in your heart that as a man disciplines his son, so Yahweh your God disciplines you.
echoes.note: The training/disciplining work of grace (v.12) echoes 'as a man chastens his son, so the LORD your God chastens you.' Reinforces the paideia background alongside Proverbs 3.

echoes.text: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh’s glory is risen on you. For, behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the peoples; but Yahweh will arise on you, and his glory shall be seen on you.
echoes.note: 'The appearing of the glory of our great God' (v.13) draws on the glory of the LORD that rises and is seen upon his people while darkness covers the earth. An eschatological epiphany-of-glory source.

echoes.text: For Yahweh has built up Zion. He has appeared in his glory.
echoes.note: 'The LORD shall appear in his glory' undergirds the 'blessed hope and appearing of the glory' (v.13). The verb of divine appearing in glory matches the epiphany expectation.

echoes.text: neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols, nor with their detestable things, nor with any of their transgressions; but I will save them out of all their dwelling places, in which they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people, and I will be their God.
echoes.note: 'Purify for himself a people' (v.14) echoes 'I will cleanse them... so they shall be my people, and I will be their God.' The cleansing-to-be-a-people motif of the new covenant underlies the purifying purpose of redemption.

echoes.text: They shall be mine,” says Yahweh of Armies, “my own possession in the day that I make, and I will spare them, as a man spares his own son who serves him.
echoes.note: 'They shall be mine, my treasured possession (peculiar treasure)' on the day God acts supports the 'people for his own possession' of v.14, joining the treasured-people motif to an eschatological day, fitting the appearing of v.13.

echoes.text: Yahweh has made bare his holy arm in the eyes of all the nations; and all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
echoes.note: Salvation 'to all men' (v.11) echoes the bared arm of the LORD by which 'all the ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God.' A faint universal-salvation echo supporting v.11.

echoes.text: “Behold, I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me; and the Lord, whom you seek, will suddenly come to his temple; and the messenger of the covenant, whom you desire, behold, he comes!” says Yahweh of Armies. “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderer’s soap;
echoes.note: The sudden coming of the Lord to his temple, and the question 'who shall abide the day of his appearing,' resonates with the awaited appearing in glory (v.13) and the purifying purpose of v.14. Contested, faint volume.

echoes.text: I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you.
echoes.note: The promise to sprinkle clean water and cleanse from all uncleanness reinforces the 'purify a people' language of v.14 within the same Ezekielian new-covenant cleansing complex. Faint, secondary to 37:23.

echoes.text: “Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the children of Israel, in that he was jealous with my jealousy among them, so that I didn’t consume the children of Israel in my jealousy. Therefore say, ‘Behold, I give to him my covenant of peace. It shall be to him, and to his seed after him, the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he was jealous for his God, and made atonement for the children of […]
echoes.note: 'Zealous for good works' (v.14) may evoke Phinehas, who 'was zealous for his God,' the paradigm of covenant zeal rewarded with an everlasting covenant. Contested, since Paul's 'zeal for good works' may be generic rather than a Phinehas allusion.

echoes.text: but because Yahweh loves you, and because he desires to keep the oath which he swore to your fathers, Yahweh has brought you out with a mighty hand, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
echoes.note: 'Redeem us' (lytroō, v.14) echoes the exodus redemption language: the LORD 'redeemed you from the house of bondage.' A faint redemption-vocabulary echo behind v.14, reinforced by Exodus 6:6.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, being small among the clans of Judah, out of you one will come out to me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings out are from of old, from ancient times.
echoes.note: Luke locates the birth in 'Bethlehem... the city of David,' the very town Micah names as the origin of the ruler 'whose goings forth are from of old.' Volume is high (the place-name itself), recurrence strong in the early-Jewish messianic reading of Micah, and thematic coherence exact: a Davidic ruler from Bethlehem. Luke leaves the citation implicit rather than quoting, but the topographic anchor is unmistakable.

echoes.text: When your days are fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your fathers, I will set up your seed after you, who shall proceed out of your bowels, and I will establish his kingdom. He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever. I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men; but my loving kindness shall not […]
echoes.note: Joseph belongs 'to the house and family of David,' and Jesus is born in David's city, activating Nathan's oracle of an everlasting Davidic throne. Coherence with Gabriel's earlier promise (1:32-33, intra-Lukan) shows Luke reading the Nathan dynastic covenant as availability; volume here is the repeated 'David' framing across vv. 4-11.

echoes.text: Yahweh said to Samuel, “How long will you mourn for Saul, since I have rejected him from being king over Israel? Fill your horn with oil, and go. I will send you to Jesse the Bethlehemite; for I have provided a king for myself among his sons.”
echoes.note: David himself was found and anointed at Bethlehem among the family of Jesse, so Bethlehem functions as the appointed site where God designates the true king over against appearances. The thematic link (humble Bethlehem origin of the LORD's chosen) is coherent, though Luke makes no verbal contact with the Samuel narrative.

echoes.text: “Sanctify to me all of the firstborn, whatever opens the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of animal. It is mine.”
echoes.note: Luke pointedly calls Jesus Mary's 'firstborn son' (prototokos), the same charged term governing the consecration of every firstborn to the LORD in Exodus. The label anticipates the redemption/presentation in vv. 22-23, so its volume is reinforced by recurrence within the chapter; coherence with the firstborn-belongs-to-God theme is high.

echoes.text: All the people who were in the gate, and the elders, said, “We are witnesses. May Yahweh make the woman who has come into your house like Rachel and like Leah, which two built the house of Israel; and treat you worthily in Ephrathah, and be famous in Bethlehem.
echoes.note: Bethlehem is the setting of Ruth, whose closing genealogy issues in David; the elders' blessing invokes building up the house of Israel in Bethlehem (Ephrathah). The connection is figural and dynastic rather than verbal, hence faint, but it belongs to the Bethlehem-David availability cluster Luke is drawing on.

echoes.text: The ox knows his owner, and the donkey his master’s crib; but Israel doesn’t know, my people don’t consider.”
echoes.note: The detail that the infant is laid in a phatne (feeding trough/manger) has long been read against Isaiah's 'the ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's manger,' a contrast between dumb beasts who recognize and an Israel that does not. The link is interpretive rather than lexically secured by Luke, so it is faint and contested, but the manger word supplies real verbal contact.

echoes.text: For to us a child is born. To us a son is given; and the government will be on his shoulders. His name will be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
echoes.note: The angel announces a child born 'this day' who is 'Savior... Christ the Lord' bringing 'great joy' and 'peace,' the cluster of Isaiah's oracle of the child born to us, called the Prince of Peace, on whose shoulder the government rests. Coherence is exact (birth, joy, peace, Davidic rule) and the theme recurs across the infancy account, giving strong volume despite no formula quotation.

echoes.text: Now therefore you shall tell my servant David this, ‘Thus says Yahweh of Armies, “I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, that you should be prince over my people, over Israel.
echoes.note: Shepherds first receive the Davidic birth announcement, fittingly because David was taken 'from following the sheep' to shepherd Israel. The motif of the shepherd-king frames the angel's proclamation of a 'Savior... in the city of David'; coherence is high, though the link is conceptual rather than quoted.

echoes.text: Yahweh’s glory settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it six days. The seventh day he called to Moses out of the midst of the cloud.
echoes.note: 'The glory of the LORD shone around them' renders the Septuagintal doxa kyriou, the visible Sinai/tabernacle glory that settled and shone. Luke uses the technical theophany vocabulary, giving real volume; coherence is high as the kabod now attends the announcement of salvation.

echoes.text: You have multiplied the nation. You have increased their joy. They rejoice before you according to the joy in harvest, as men rejoice when they divide the plunder.
echoes.note: 'Good news of great joy' echoes Isaiah's 'they rejoice before you... as men rejoice when they divide the spoil,' the joy attending the breaking of the oppressor's yoke in the same Immanuel oracle that names the child. The joy-language strengthens the broader Isaiah 9 allusion in this pericope.

echoes.text: How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace, who brings good news of good, who publishes salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns!”
echoes.note: The angel 'brings good news' (euangelizomai) of peace and salvation, the very verb-and-content of Isaiah's herald who publishes peace and announces 'your God reigns.' Septuagintal availability is direct and the salvation/peace coherence is strong; Luke universalizes it to 'all the people.'

echoes.text: You, tower of the flock, the hill of the daughter of Zion, to you it will come, yes, the former dominion will come, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.
echoes.note: The shepherds 'keeping watch over their flock' near Bethlehem evoke Micah's 'tower of the flock' (Migdal Eder), traditionally located by Bethlehem and read messianically as the place where kingship returns. Verbal contact is slight in Greek, so the echo is faint, but the Bethlehem-shepherd-king geography is thematically coherent.

echoes.text: Yahweh will give strength to his people. Yahweh will bless his people with peace.
echoes.note: The Gloria's 'on earth peace' set beside the heavenly host's praise recalls the psalm in which the LORD enthroned amid the heavenly beings 'gives strength to his people' and 'blesses his people with peace.' The host-of-heaven plus peace pairing is coherent though the verbal contact is thin, so it is a faint supporting echo.

echoes.text: One called to another, and said, “Holy, holy, holy, is Yahweh of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!”
echoes.note: The 'multitude of the heavenly army' crying 'Glory to God in the highest' resembles the seraphim antiphon 'Holy... the whole earth is full of his glory,' a heavenly liturgy proclaiming God's glory over the earth. The pattern (angelic chorus, glory, earth) is coherent though Luke's wording is independent.

echoes.text: Praise Yah! Praise Yahweh from the heavens! Praise him in the heights! Praise him, all his angels! Praise him, all his army!
echoes.note: 'Glory to God in the highest' with the angelic host praising parallels the psalm's call to 'praise him in the heights... praise him, all his hosts/angels.' The heights/host/praise vocabulary is coherent, supplying a plausible liturgical backdrop to the Gloria, though faint as direct source.

echoes.text: Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brothers: and the Spirit of Yahweh came mightily on David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.
echoes.note: Naming Jesus 'Savior... Christ (anointed) the Lord' in David's city recalls the anointing of David at Bethlehem when the Spirit rushed upon him. The christos-David-Bethlehem nexus is coherent within the chapter's Davidic frame, though no verbal echo is pressed.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light.
To us a child is born.
The grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all.
To us a child is born.
Glory to God in the highest, and peace on earth.
Come, let us adore him. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: It is night, and the fields are cold, and ordinary people are keeping watch.
Glory to God in the highest!
Suddenly the dark is torn open with light, and the sky is loud with song.
Glory to God in the highest!
To you is born this day a Savior — wrapped in cloth, laid in a feeding trough.
Glory to God in the highest!
The great light has come to the smallest place; God is here, and God is for us.
Glory to God in the highest, and peace on earth!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: A great light for those in darkness; to us a child is born.
Glory to God in the highest!
Grace has appeared, a Savior in a manger.
Glory to God in the highest!
God comes to the smallest place; come, adore him.
Glory to God in the highest! Amen.
